gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-tagbanw: Raw and jostling, Disorder spaces its glyphs far apart and gives its crossbars the same heft as its stems. But shrink it down and that roughness fades, while Noto Sans Tagbanwa keeps its open curves clear.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-tai-vie: One unbroken stroke weight runs through every Disorder letter, with no swelling at the joins. And Noto Sans Tai Viet, with its short ascenders and big x-height, can be sized up without crowding.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-tc: Noto Sans TC reads generously, with large counters and curves that swing outward instead of curling in. And Disorder, its r, n and m arches matching their stems, gives that openness something rougher to lean on.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-thaana: Disorder draws a single line weight with no swelling at the joins, loud and raw up top. Noto Sans Thaana does the opposite job, with wide channels into each counter that keep lowercase forms big and open.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-thai-lo: Noto Sans Thai Looped looks bold, since its lowercase bodies run so large. Disorder is the one for raw, rod-stiff headings, every horizontal and vertical identical in thickness, while the body font's spacious curve gaps handle the reading.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Rough, spaced-out and hairline-free, that's Disorder up top. Noto Sans Tirhuta, with its dominant x-height and terminals cut back to leave big gaps, should keep running text feeling open and unhurried, page after page.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-ugariti: Raw and loosely strung, Disorder has no stroke modulation at all and glyphs set well apart. But Noto Sans Ugaritic leaves its letter mouths open and keeps x-height close to cap height, so text should flow smoothly.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Disorder's stroke ends all look cut from one ribbon. Noto Sans Wancho brings a hulking, chalk-thick lowercase and an e with a wide terminal gap, which gives the rough heading a sturdy partner on the page.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-zanabaz: Noto Sans Zanabazar Square has a soaring x-height and wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp. Noto Sans Zanabazar Square then sits beneath Disorder, whose single thick-thread stroke and spaced-out glyphs supply the noise.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-traditional-: Disorder draws every line with a constant-width pen, no swelling where curves meet stems, and its glyphs sit well apart. Use it big and brief, while Noto Traditional Nushu takes the rest.
